dispositions.rationale: Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A28 judges the skill text as S3.4's deliverable and F1 to F7 judge the writer's behaviour under BRF-A16 to BRF-A20; neither claims the other (merged record, behavioural-outcome-1).

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A24 observes the behaviour the constraint protects, that the helper runs where nothing third-party is importable; an optional import that changes nothing observable is a code-review read, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-10 rules for a second resolver.
Repeats obligation-reduction-5 of the merged record: the installer stages the skill directory whole, and the evaluation runs the skill from source by full path (BRF-D8).
The installer prunes every test file and every evals/ directory by its own .installignore, and that staging check is the installer's gate, outside this spec's scope.
The sentence is agents-config-9k9.405.9's deliverable, and BRF-D6's 'leaves it alone' is a scope boundary, not a preservation obligation; that item's own criteria hold the sentence in place.
Repeats obligation-reduction-11 of the merged record: content-lint measures every deployed skill body against its cap and fails the gate above it, and S3.4's continuation requires that gate green.

Repeats obligation-reduction-1 of the merged record: the per-brief guard is check (BRF-A8, BRF-A23), which BRF-A28 makes the skill require before every dispatch; the evaluation claims fidelity over its fixtures under the stochastic rule.
Repeats obligation-reduction-2 of the merged record: evidence fidelity in any brief is what check --checks decides (BRF-A23).
Repeats obligation-reduction-3 of the merged record: the writer sees one refusal shape whatever the code; F3 to F5 sample the refusal sources, and BRF-A28 reads the relay instruction in the skill.

F6 samples the writer's judgment on one infeasible check, and judging feasibility in code is out of scope by the spec's own list; BRF-D8 states that the runs measure the scope sentence and never prove it.
Repeats obligation-reduction-12 of the merged record: the attestation is the record; the tree cannot observe the execution it attests (BRF-D8).
Repeats obligation-reduction-13 of the merged record: BRF-D8 states the repeat limit is an operator procedure because no output shows a retry.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run, output, report or attempt that was never committed, or one replaced before commit.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run, output, report or attempt that was never committed, or one replaced before commit. The record names the outputs that count and BRF-A35 refuses a sixth.

The fingerprint excludes evals/, so a scorer change alters no fingerprint and BRF-A33 keeps every lock current or fallen on its stored runs; whether the operator dispatches writers anyway is an act the tree cannot observe.

Reading a failed run and judging it a defect is the operator's act. BRF-D8 states the response, changing the skill, which voids the lock, as procedure, and the scope excludes judging in code what only a reading decides.

BRF-A27, BRF-A32 and BRF-A35 pin the scorer's verdict for every state BRF-D8 defines, a side at five, four, three or fewer of five, its second five, a refused record; a scorer that invents a state the spec lacks is a code-review read, and 'changing a threshold amends this spec' binds the author, whom no test observes.

The gate clauses live in the Continuations lines because the work facade requires them there; a numbered criterion that restated 'make ci exits 0' would judge the gate rather than the behaviour, which the acceptance-criteria standard forbids, and BRF-A31 pins that each gate reads the suites.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-D2 gives the spec source's syntax as the pair `--spec PATH --ids ID,...`, so `--spec` alone is a malformed invocation of that source for S3.1's argument parsing to refuse, and BRF-A3's empty ID list is the `--ids` given empty; the earlier round ruled the same for `--ids` beside another source (brief5 what-if-2).

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A25 obliges one refusal naming every fault the helper detects, whatever their codes; its two absent IDs are an instance of the obligation, not its bound, and BRF-D4 states the aggregation rule the criterion observes.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: a fenced line never opens or continues an entry under rule 5, so in a criteria file it is a nonblank line outside an entry, which BRF-A7 refuses as malformed-criteria naming the line and, by its own second sentence, never as no-criteria; the outcome is decided.

parts.statement: The criteria section contains exactly the assigned spec, criteria-file or rendered-item entries, with full source text.
Non-refusal output has the criteria and evidence sections, and no third section.
The full criteria section is identical across absent, complete and incomplete check plans.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "Its emit mode prints exactly two Markdown sections." BRF-D2 names the three sources. BRF-D5: "The criteria section is the same whether --checks is absent, complete or leaves a criterion unready."
obligations.statement: emit produces the assigned criteria and a separate evidence section without changing criteria according to check readiness.

parts.statement: Entries are read according to the five grammar rules, with the heading requirement omitted for criteria files.
Both parsers identify their counterpart; both suites read the shared expected readings, reject an absent fixture and expose a rule-breaking helper variant for every rule.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "Spec and file entries follow spec-lint's entry grammar, joined text included." "One fixture keeps the two readings from drifting apart unseen." "Both suites fail when the fixture is absent."
obligations.statement: Spec and criteria-file parsing follows the shared entry grammar, and a shared fixture exposes rule-breaking parser variants and absent-fixture failures.

parts.statement: emit and check refuse as source-conflict for absent or multiple source flags, naming the flags given.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "Exactly one source flag is given. More than one, or none, refuses as source-conflict."
obligations.statement: Exactly one source flag is accepted; otherwise the helper refuses and names the supplied flags.

parts.statement: Empty assignments and blank criteria files refuse as no-criteria; empty item rendering does likewise.
Absent assigned spec IDs refuse as unretrievable and name the IDs.
Unreadable specs, criteria files, checks files and briefs refuse as unreadable-source with the required path and assigned IDs.
Duplicate assignments or source definitions refuse as duplicate-id and name the ID.
Nonblank criteria-file lines outside entries refuse as malformed-criteria, name the line and do not also report no-criteria.
Checks files violating the specified JSON shape refuse as malformed-checks.
Unavailable or failing item rendering refuses as render-failed, naming the item and cause.
A refusal aggregates every detected fault in readable sources, including multiple absent IDs.

obligations.source: BRF-D4: "emit prints nothing on stdout and one JSON object on stderr naming each fault, and exits 2." Its fault list and aggregation paragraphs define the cases.
obligations.statement: Refusals replace pasteable output with one fault-reporting JSON object on stderr and exit 2, using the specified fault codes and details.

parts.statement: Complete plans produce exactly the assigned evidence entries and exit 0; well-formed unassigned entries have no effect.
Missing checks and absent or whitespace-only fields produce the specified unready reasons, stderr IDs and exit 1; absent --checks makes every ID unready.
Shape validation applies to every entry; absent observe/pass keys are blank rather than malformed, and other keys have no effect.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 defines the checks-file shape, blank fields, ignored keys and entries, closed reason set, and exit-1 behavior.
obligations.statement: Evidence maps every assigned ID to its observation and pass rule or to the specified unready reasons.

parts.statement: Without --checks, check accepts preserved criteria and rejects every missing, added or altered ID under BRF-D3.
With --checks, check accepts only preserved criteria and evidence and identifies missing, added or altered evidence IDs.
check reports shared-source failures as emit would and refuses unreadable briefs.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "Its check mode compares a written brief with the source, and with the plan when given --checks." BRF-D3 defines exact ID sets and whitespace-normalized text, with order ignored.
obligations.statement: check verifies criteria fidelity and, when supplied a plan, evidence fidelity, while sharing emit's source failures.

parts.statement: emit and check work without importable third-party packages and match their uv-run stdout, stderr and exit status.
The helper uses no third-party package, including an optional package when available.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "The helper uses the standard library only, so it runs under uv run or python3 on every supported tool."
obligations.statement: The helper uses only the standard library and runs equivalently under python3 and uv run.

parts.statement: The helper, helper tests, shared fixture, evaluation fixtures, scorer and spec-lint fixture test are delivered at their prescribed locations.
Installer output excludes evals/ and all test files, so neither suite runs in a deployed tree.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "The skill ships brief_criteria.py beside its SKILL.md." BRF-D2 locates the shared fixture in evals/ and requires pruning every test file. BRF-D8 locates fixtures and evals/score_briefs.py there. The ordered slices name the helper and fixture-test locations.
obligations.statement: The deliverables occupy the specified source layout, while tests and evaluations are excluded from deployed trees.

parts.statement: The skill text and skeleton instruct unchanged helper-section pasting, checking before dispatch, and reporting refusal or unready criteria instead of dispatching.
The existing LIFE-A32 re-attack sentence remains unchanged.
The rewritten skill respects content-lint's token caps.

obligations.source: BRF-D6 requires emit, unchanged pasting, check before dispatch and reporting refusal or unready criteria. It says this slice "leaves" LIFE-A32's sentence "alone" and that "Content-lint's token caps apply."
obligations.statement: The skill's acceptance-criteria instructions and skeleton route through the helper, preserve the existing re-attack sentence and respect token caps.

parts.statement: The successful F1/F2 outputs required by the current preservation locks preserve their assigned criteria.
All other generated dispatches preserve their assigned criteria, including other assignments, subsequent runs and failure runs permitted within a lock.
The successful F1/F2 outputs required by the current evidence locks preserve their planned evidence separately from criterion text.
All other generated dispatches preserve their planned evidence separately from criterion text.
The successful F3/F4/F5 outputs required by their current locks report the specified helper refusal without dispatching a brief.
Every other helper refusal is relayed to the requester without dispatch, including other refusal classes and failure runs permitted within a lock.
The successful F6/F7 outputs required by their current locks report the specified unready IDs without dispatching a brief.
Every other criterion lacking a feasible planned check is judged and reported unready without dispatch.

obligations.source: Scope: "A dispatch brief must carry exactly the criteria assigned to the work. It must refuse when it cannot. It must map each criterion to its planned check, apart from the criterion's text. A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready." BRF-D4 and BRF-D5 require reporting instead of dispatching.
obligations.statement: Generated dispatch briefs preserve criteria and evidence; writers report refusals and infeasible checks instead of dispatching.

parts.statement: The actual executions use the required model, native Agent tool, fresh contexts, source-tree skill by full path, fixed tasks and no subagent tool.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "The writer is Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, given the skill from the source tree by full path." Each fixture uses a fixed task; the writer has no subagent tool; runs use fresh contexts.
obligations.statement: Evaluation outputs are actually produced under the prescribed writer execution protocol.

parts.statement: The evaluation of record has the required current locks for F1 through F7, using their specified success conditions.
The scorer rejects violating seeded outputs, including invalid forms, and distinguishes F1/F2's two sides.

obligations.source: BRF-D8's fixture table, its Form-line requirement, its report-form definition, and: "evals/score_briefs.py scores the outputs mechanically, and scores F1's and F2's preservation and evidence separately."
obligations.statement: The evaluation mechanically scores the seven prescribed fixtures, recognizes output forms and scores F1/F2 preservation and evidence separately.

parts.statement: Missing first-five outputs, missing named files or required record metadata make the fixture incomplete rather than failed or locked, with missing outputs named pending.
The record names a Claude Opus resolved model ID, fingerprint and operator attestations before the fixture can lock.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 requires the record to name the resolved model ID and attest fresh contexts and the native Agent tool; missing outputs stay pending. It requires fingerprints and counted-output identification.
obligations.statement: Incomplete evaluation evidence cannot establish a lock, and the record carries required execution metadata.

parts.statement: An absent first-five output remains pending and prevents a lock rather than counting as a failed run.
The operator repeats a no-output run at most twice.
The existing incomplete attempt is completed in place and is never replaced.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A run with no output is repeated at most twice. It is then left pending and never scored as failed." "An incomplete attempt is completed in place ... and it is never replaced."
obligations.statement: No-output runs receive bounded repeats, remain pending when exhausted, and incomplete attempts are completed in place rather than replaced.

parts.statement: Five-of-five sides pass, two-or-fewer sides fail, and three-or-four sides await their second five without being locked, failed or incomplete.
An earned second five locks the fixture only when each affected side reaches eight passes across ten; otherwise it fails.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: five passes pass; three or four passes earn a second five and require eight of ten; two or fewer fail; every side must pass for a fixture to lock.
obligations.statement: Every fixture side follows the prescribed five-run and earned-second-five decision rule.

parts.statement: More than five named first-stage or second-stage outputs are refused and reported incomplete; unnamed extra outputs do not affect scoring.
Every attempt's outputs, record and report are retained and committed at the prescribed location, including failed, incomplete and unnamed late outputs and earned second fives.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 says the record names the counted outputs, unnamed late arrivals stay committed but score nothing, excess named runs are refused, and attempts are committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/ with outputs, record and report whatever they show.
obligations.statement: Records select the counted outputs within the prescribed limits, while all attempt evidence remains committed.

parts.statement: Mismatched fingerprints are not current, matching passing locks count, matching failing locks fall, and changes outside the fingerprint do not invalidate a passing lock.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines fingerprints from the skill directory without evals/, fixture files and resolved model ID, and requires stored-output rescoring after scorer changes.
obligations.statement: The evaluation of record contains only current locks whose fingerprints match and whose stored runs pass the current scorer.

parts.statement: The scorer scores the earlier committed attempt and refuses a later committed attempt with the same fingerprint in every earlier-result state.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "The scorer refuses a second attempt recording a fingerprint it has already seen, whether the earlier locked, failed or stayed incomplete."
obligations.statement: A fingerprint receives only one committed attempt, regardless of whether that attempt locked, failed or remained incomplete.

parts.statement: Only fixtures with changed fingerprints dispatch writers again, and scorer-only changes dispatch none.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A change voids only the locks whose fingerprint it alters, and only those fixtures run again." "A change to the scorer dispatches no writer."
obligations.statement: Writer reruns are limited to invalidated fixtures; scorer-only changes cause rescoring without writer dispatch.

parts.statement: Demonstrated defects behind locks receive the required skill correction, lock invalidation and fixture rerun.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A failed run behind a lock is committed and read like any other, and a defect it shows is answered by changing the skill, which voids the lock and runs the fixture again."
obligations.statement: A defect demonstrated by a failed run behind a lock is answered by changing the skill and rerunning the affected fixture.

parts.statement: The spec is amended whenever an evaluation run count or threshold changes.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "Changing a run count or threshold amends this spec."
obligations.statement: Changes to evaluation run counts or thresholds are accompanied by a spec amendment.

parts.statement: Repeated unchanged helper executions have identical stdout, stderr and exit status, write no files and share nothing across concurrent different-source runs.

obligations.source: What-if questions: "emit and check read and never write, so running either twice or with nothing changed prints the same result and concurrent runs share nothing."
obligations.statement: Helper executions are read-only, repeatable and isolated from concurrent executions.

parts.statement: content-tests runs the helper and scorer suites, ci runs the spec-lint fixture test, and seeded failures make their gates red.
The required unseeded content-tests, ci and content-lint gates exit 0 for the delivery slices that require them.

obligations.source: BRF-D9: "The helper suites establish the mechanism." The Continuations require make content-tests and make ci to exit 0 for S3.1, make content-tests for S3.2/S3.3, and make content-lint for S3.4.
obligations.statement: The required delivery gates exercise the relevant suites and pass for their slices.

ground.reason: BRF-D6 promises that the skill routes the writer through emit and check before dispatch. BRF-A28 verifies only that four instructions appear in the skill text. The generated-brief evaluation checks returned content, but does not establish that the writer followed this route.

objections.objection: The content test can accept the skill while the writer produces matching sections by hand and dispatches without running check.
objections.obligation: BRF-D6's requirement that criteria and evidence come from emit and that check runs before dispatch.

scenario.expect: The content test passes because all four instructions appear. F1 and F2 can also pass their output checks, while the writer never invokes emit or check before dispatch.
scenario.given: A skill containing every instruction required by BRF-A28, whose writer manually reproduces the correct criteria and evidence sections.
scenario.when: BRF-A28's content test reads the skill and the generated-brief evaluation scores the writer's outputs.

ground.reason: BRF-D1 says, "The helper uses the standard library only." BRF-A24 checks independence from installed third-party packages and equality across runtimes. It does not exclude optional third-party imports.

objections.objection: The helper can use an optional third-party package while satisfying the runtime comparison.

scenario.expect: Both runtimes produce identical results and every criterion passes, although the uv execution uses a third-party package.
scenario.given: The helper optionally imports a third-party package and uses an equivalent standard-library fallback when that package is unavailable.
scenario.when: BRF-A24 compares emit and check under python3 and uv run.

ground.reason: BRF-D1 promises that "The skill ships brief_criteria.py beside its SKILL.md." BRF-D2 and BRF-D8 also prescribe fixture and scorer locations. The criteria observe their behavior and contents, without checking the promised source layout.

objections.objection: A working helper and evaluation can pass their checks while the skill lacks the helper at its promised location.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes using explicit paths, but the delivered skill directory lacks brief_criteria.py beside SKILL.md.
scenario.given: The helper is stored elsewhere, and the suites and evaluation invoke that location explicitly.
scenario.when: The helper, content tests and generated-brief evaluation run.

ground.reason: BRF-D2 states, "The installer prunes every test file along with evals/, so neither suite ever runs in a deployed tree." No criterion checks deployed-tree contents or exclusion of those suites.

objections.objection: Tests and evaluation files can be deployed despite all source-tree checks passing.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the deployed skill contains test files or evals/ and can run a suite there.
scenario.given: The source-tree implementation satisfies the helper and scorer criteria, while installer staging retains the test artifacts.
scenario.when: The skill is staged for deployment.

ground.reason: BRF-D6 says that LIFE-A32's sentence "belongs to lifecycle S6 ... so this slice leaves it alone." BRF-A28 reads four routing instructions and does not check preservation of that sentence.

objections.objection: The skill rewrite can remove or change the existing re-attack sentence.

scenario.expect: The content test and all evaluations pass, although the existing re-attack sentence has changed.
scenario.given: The rewritten skill contains all four BRF-A28 instructions but removes LIFE-A32's sentence.
scenario.when: The skill's content test and evaluation run.

ground.reason: BRF-D6 states, "Content-lint's token caps apply." No numbered criterion checks the skill against those caps. Reading routing instructions does not establish compliance.

objections.objection: The rewritten skill can exceed its token cap.

scenario.expect: Every numbered criterion passes, but content-lint rejects the skill for exceeding its token cap.
scenario.given: The skill contains the required instructions and enough additional text to exceed its cap.
scenario.when: The content test and generated-brief evaluation run.

ground.reason: Scope says, "A dispatch brief must carry exactly the criteria assigned to the work." BRF-A16 establishes the required successful F1/F2 observations. Its locks permit failed runs and cover no other assignments.

objections.objection: A writer can earn current preservation locks while producing another brief with changed or missing criteria.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes and the current locks stand, but a returned brief omits an assigned criterion.
scenario.given: The writer meets the F1/F2 lock thresholds but mishandles an assignment outside those fixtures.
scenario.when: The writer returns a brief for that assignment.

ground.reason: Scope says, "It must map each criterion to its planned check, apart from the criterion's text." BRF-D3 requires exact evidence IDs and entries. BRF-A17 covers only the successful observations required by the fixed F1/F2 evaluation.

objections.objection: A writer can earn evidence locks while producing another brief with missing or altered evidence.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the new brief associates a criterion with a different pass rule from its plan.
scenario.given: The writer meets the F1/F2 evidence thresholds but rewords evidence on another assignment.
scenario.when: The writer returns that assignment's brief.

ground.reason: Scope requires refusal when the brief cannot carry its assigned criteria. BRF-D4 says the writer must "relay a refusal to its requester and dispatch nothing." BRF-A18 and BRF-A19 sample only no-criteria, unretrievable and unreadable-spec refusals, with thresholds that permit failed runs.

objections.objection: The writer can dispatch after a refusal outside the successful F3/F4/F5 observations.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the writer returns a brief after the helper refuses.
scenario.given: The writer passes the fixed refusal fixtures but ignores a duplicate-id refusal.
scenario.when: The writer briefs work whose source defines an assigned ID twice.

ground.reason: Scope says, "A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready." BRF-D5 assigns feasibility judgment to the writer. BRF-A20 samples one subjective check and two missing or blank checks; it does not cover other infeasible checks or require every sampled run to succeed.

objections.objection: The writer can pass F6/F7 while dispatching a criterion with another infeasible check.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the writer returns a brief without reporting the infeasible criterion as unready.
scenario.given: The writer recognizes F6's wording and F7's missing fields but accepts a nonblank check requiring access to an unavailable private system.
scenario.when: The writer assesses and briefs that criterion.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 requires Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, fresh contexts, the source-tree skill by full path, fixed tasks and no subagent tool. BRF-A26 checks recorded model identity and attestations. Those artifacts do not establish the actual execution protocol.

objections.objection: Valid-looking records can establish locks for outputs produced under a different execution protocol.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes and the scorer locks the fixtures, although their outputs were not produced through the required protocol.
scenario.given: Stored outputs satisfy the fixtures, and their records name Claude Opus and attest fresh contexts and the native Agent tool, but the outputs were generated in one reused context using another route.
scenario.when: The scorer validates the records and outputs.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 says, "A run with no output is repeated at most twice." It expressly calls the limit an operator procedure. BRF-A26 checks missing-output classification, not the number of retries performed.

objections.objection: The operator can exceed the retry limit without failing a criterion.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the attempt includes an output obtained after more than two repeats.
scenario.given: A dispatch returns no output, and the operator repeats it three times before obtaining an otherwise passing output.
scenario.when: The operator records that output and the scorer evaluates the attempt.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 says an incomplete attempt "is completed in place ... and it is never replaced." BRF-A34 rejects two committed attempts with the same fingerprint. It does not reject replacement of the sole recorded attempt.

objections.objection: An incomplete attempt can be replaced while the scorer sees only one attempt for its fingerprint.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, although the original incomplete attempt was replaced.
scenario.given: An incomplete attempt exists, and the operator overwrites its record and outputs with a new execution under the same fingerprint.
scenario.when: The scorer reads the resulting single attempt.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 requires an attempt to be committed "with its outputs, its record and its report, whatever it shows," and says an unnamed late arrival "stays committed and scores nothing." BRF-A26 and BRF-A35 check named-output presence and selection, without requiring preservation and commitment of all evidence.

objections.objection: Passing attempts can omit their report, unscored outputs or committed evidence.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the late output and attempt report are absent from committed evidence.
scenario.given: An attempt has its named passing outputs and valid record; a repeated run later produces an unnamed output.
scenario.when: The operator discards the late output and omits the report while retaining everything the scorer reads.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 states that "only those fixtures run again" whose fingerprints change, and "A change to the scorer dispatches no writer." BRF-A33 checks lock currency and rescoring results, without observing dispatch activity.

objections.objection: Unnecessary writer dispatches can occur while lock and rescoring checks remain correct.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes and stored outputs are rescored correctly, but new writers are dispatched for unchanged fixtures.
scenario.given: Only scorer code changes, and all fixture fingerprints remain unchanged.
scenario.when: The operator dispatches additional writers, leaves their outputs unscored, and runs the scorer over the stored attempts.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 says a defect shown by a failed run behind a lock "is answered by changing the skill, which voids the lock and runs the fixture again." The lock criteria permit retained failed runs and do not require that corrective action.

objections.objection: A demonstrated skill defect can remain unanswered behind a current lock.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes and the fixture remains locked, but the demonstrated skill defect receives no change or rerun.
scenario.given: A side scores four of five, then four of its second five; one failed output demonstrates a skill defect.
scenario.when: The scorer locks the side at eight of ten and the operator leaves the skill unchanged.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 states, "Changing a run count or threshold amends this spec." No criterion observes whether the evaluation policy and spec are amended together.

objections.objection: The evaluation policy can change for cases outside the prescribed scorer examples without an accompanying spec amendment.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's stated checks pass, but the scorer applies an undocumented threshold exception.
scenario.given: The scorer retains all prescribed behavior for the checked scenarios but adds a different threshold for an untested record condition.
scenario.when: An attempt with that condition is evaluated without amending the spec.

ground.reason: The Continuations require make content-tests and make ci to exit 0, and S3.4 requires make content-lint to exit 0. BRF-A31 establishes suite wiring and propagation of seeded failures. It does not require successful unseeded gate results.

objections.objection: The numbered criteria can be satisfied while a required delivery gate remains red.

scenario.expect: Every numbered criterion's check passes, but the standalone delivery gate exits nonzero.
scenario.given: The specified helper, scorer and fixture checks pass, while another check in a required gate fails.
scenario.when: The required gate runs over the delivery tree.

ground.reason: BRF-A27's lock condition names only the output set, while BRF-A26 lists record conditions (model ID, fingerprint, operator attestation) that make an attempt incomplete; the set never states whether A27's lock is conditioned on A26's completeness requirements.

objections.objection: A fixture whose sides all pass but whose record lacks the operator attestation or resolved model ID is locked under one reading of BRF-A27 and incomplete under BRF-A26, so the same attempt lands both inside and outside the evaluation of record depending on which criterion the judge applies.

scenario.expect: Under BRF-A27's wording ('Given a set in which every side passes all five of its runs, it locks every fixture') the fixtures lock; under BRF-A26 the same attempt is incomplete and names each missing output as pending, and the fixture never locks. The two verdicts conflict.
scenario.given: A committed attempt in which every side of every fixture passes all five of its runs, but the attempt's record carries no operator attestation of fresh contexts and the native Agent tool (or no resolved model ID).
scenario.when: The scorer evaluates the attempt and the result is judged against the criteria.

ground.reason: BRF-A3 requires a no-criteria refusal for an empty ID list, and BRF-D2/BRF-A29 require source-conflict when no source flag is given, but nothing states whether --ids is mandatory with --spec, so '--spec PATH' alone (or --ids with an empty value) has no decided reading.

objections.objection: An invocation of emit with --spec and no --ids (or an empty --ids value) admits three materially different outcomes — a no-criteria refusal, a source-conflict refusal, or emitting every criterion in the spec — and the criteria do not say which the helper must produce.

scenario.expect: One reading treats --ids as given-but-empty and expects the BRF-A3 no-criteria refusal; another treats the assignment as unspecified and expects the BRF-A29 source-conflict refusal; a third reads --spec alone as assigning the spec's criteria and expects sections on stdout with exit 0. Each reading produces a different exit status and stderr object.
scenario.given: A readable, well-formed spec whose acceptance-criteria section holds entries, and emit invoked as 'emit --spec PATH' with --ids omitted entirely, or with an empty ID list.
scenario.when: The helper runs and its refusal code (or lack of refusal) is judged against the criteria.

ground.reason: BRF-D4 states one refusal names every fault the helper detects in the sources it can read, but the only aggregation criterion (BRF-A25) tests two faults of the same code (`unretrievable` twice). No criterion checks that faults of different codes aggregate into one refusal.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a helper that drops or splits faults when they carry different refusal codes — e.g., it could report only the unreadable checks file and stay silent on the absent IDs, or emit two separate refusals, and every criterion still passes.

scenario.expect: One JSON refusal on stderr carrying `unreadable-source` for the checks path plus `unretrievable` naming both IDs, exit 2, no stdout — which no criterion tests
scenario.given: A spec missing two assigned IDs and a `--checks` file that does not exist, all in one `emit` invocation
scenario.when: `emit` runs and detects the unreadable checks file and the two absent spec IDs

ground.reason: Grammar rule 5 says a fenced line never opens or continues an entry, while `malformed-criteria` fires on any nonblank line outside an entry. For a criteria file (which follows every rule but the second, so fences are still recognised), the two rules give different answers for fence content, and no criterion pins which refusal results.

objections.objection: The criteria let through either behaviour for fenced content in a criteria file — refuse as `malformed-criteria`, or ignore the fence and refuse as `no-criteria` — and the two refusals tell the writer different faults, so an implementation can pick the misleading one and still pass every criterion.

scenario.expect: A single, decided refusal — either `malformed-criteria` naming the fence line or `no-criteria` with the fence ignored — which no criterion or decision rules out or fixes
scenario.given: A criteria file whose only nonblank lines are a fenced code block (fence markers and contents)
scenario.when: `emit --criteria FILE` runs
